import pytest

from datekit.calendar import day_of_year, days_in_month, is_leap_year


def test_common_leap_years():
    assert is_leap_year(2024)
    assert not is_leap_year(2023)


def test_century_years():
    # Divisible by 100 is not a leap year, unless also divisible by 400.
    assert not is_leap_year(1900)
    assert is_leap_year(2000)


def test_days_in_month():
    assert days_in_month(2024, 2) == 29
    assert days_in_month(2023, 2) == 28
    assert days_in_month(2023, 12) == 31
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        days_in_month(2023, 13)


def test_day_of_year():
    assert day_of_year(2023, 1, 1) == 1
    assert day_of_year(2024, 12, 31) == 366
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        day_of_year(2023, 2, 29)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("year", "expected"),
    [(1600, True), (1700, False), (1800, False), (1900, False), (2000, True), (2100, False), (2400, True)],
)
def test_gregorian_century_rule(year, expected):
    assert is_leap_year(year) is expected


def test_february_in_century_years():
    assert days_in_month(1900, 2) == 28
    assert days_in_month(2000, 2) == 29

tester.explanation: Adds a parametrized test of the Gregorian century rule and checks February lengths in 1900 and 2000.

debugger.diagnosis: The patch only checks divisibility by 400, so ordinary leap years such as 2024 are no longer leap years: test_common_leap_years, test_days_in_month and test_day_of_year fail. The rule needs all three conditions: divisible by 4, and not a century unless divisible by 400.
debugger.explanation: Use the complete Gregorian rule: year % 4 == 0 and (year % 100 != 0 or year % 400 == 0).

reviewer.summary: Fixes is_leap_year to follow the Gregorian calendar: years divisible by 100 are leap years only when divisible by 400. Adds parametrized tests for century years and February lengths. All 22 tests, the security scan and static analysis pass.
concerns: Behaviour changes for century years (e.g. 1900, 2100): days_in_month and day_of_year now return 28/365-based values there, which is correct but visible to callers.
suggested_followups: Consider validating that year is positive; the Gregorian rule is not meaningful before 1582.
